speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if you have had any recent injuries or insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear a pop or feel a snapping sensation at the moment of injury, and are you currently unable to actively bend or straighten the fingertip? Please also inspect the tip of the finger for any visible skin breaks or abrasions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your inability to flex the fingertip and the extended resting position, this strongly suggests a flexor tendon injury. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_of_right_hand.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since there is no fracture, the mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the fingertip strongly point to an avulsion of the flexor tendon. Do you have any difficulty flexing the other joints of that finger, or is the dysfunction isolated strictly to the very tip?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The injury mechanism and inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint are classic for a Jersey Finger. Is your inability to flex isolated strictly to the tip of the finger, or can you also flex the middle joint of that finger normally?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you make a fist and check if your right ring finger remains extended at the tip while the other fingers curl in? This specific deformity confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
